result.summary: Check LevelDB iterator status in `txindex` during transaction lookups via `FindTx()`. It adds a `CDBIterator::CheckStatus()` helper that invokes `HandleError()` if an iterator encountered an underlying database error, throwing a `dbwrapper_error` instead of silently returning `nullopt`.
result.problem: When LevelDB encounters a database corruption or I/O error during a `txindex` iterator scan, the iterator becomes invalid. Because `FindTx()` only checked whether the iterator was valid rather than inspecting its status, underlying database read errors were indistinguishable from an absent transaction and returned `nullopt` instead of alerting the caller to a database failure.
evidence: PR description: 'LevelDB detected the corruption, but the same lookup returned `nullopt` instead of throwing. Restoring the original data made the lookup work again.'
Follow-up to merged PR #35728 ('rpc: Properly throw on internal I/O errors in GetTransaction').
result.scope_notes: Small 6-line change touching dbwrapper and txindex.
result.card: txindex's FindTx method now checks LevelDB iterator error status before returning nullopt on lookup failure. Previously, if database corruption or an I/O error caused the iterator to fail, FindTx treated the transaction as simply not found rather than raising a database error. This follows up on PR 35728, which fixed similar error suppression in GetTransaction RPC handling.

risk.why: A bug in error checking could falsely throw dbwrapper_error on normal missing transaction lookups, aborting RPC or node operations.
